producer_report.summary:
Added `athena measure-build`. It builds the workspace cold in two detached git worktrees of HEAD, each with its own target directory. It commits one `athena.build-measurement/1` record under `records/build-measurements/` holding T (bytes of the first target directory), S (tracked-file bytes of a worktree), both build wall times, and the sccache hit and miss counts of each build (or `NotInstalled`). The cargo and sccache work sits behind a `CargoBuilder` trait, so tests use a fake builder. Worktrees and target directories are removed on every path, and a failed build or unreadable sccache counts write no record.

The Hestia sweep runs the measurement when no record exists and again when the `Cargo.lock` blob id at HEAD differs from the latest record's. The trigger sits in `hestia_sweep_with` (via `hestia_sweep_measuring`) and not in `review_passes`, so `athena drain` never waits for two builds.

`athena status` prints a `build      measurement:` line with the latest T, S, build times and cache figures, or "none yet". `athena measure-build` is registered in main.rs with help text, and the A1 docs and CHANGELOG say the figures come from records. No measurement was run and no figure is written.

I did not edit the A1 docs-only text beyond rewriting it, and no `athena.toml`, `defaults.toml`, workflow or drain test was touched.

open_issues: Criterion 3 says `run_sweep` runs the measurement. `run_sweep` is a pure function over `Check`s with no records access, so the trigger is `Athena::measure_build_pass`, reached through `hestia_sweep_with` -> `hestia_sweep_measuring`, and the test drives that entry. Departs from the letter, not the intent.

I changed two files outside the brief's list, as the plan said: crates/athena-core/src/store.rs (Records.build_measurements, a load arm, sort, has_record_id; without it Records::load panics on the new record kind) and crates/athena-cli/src/display.rs (prints the status line). I also added a new test file crates/athena-cli/tests/status_build_measurement.rs for the display check.
A measurement that fails (cargo error, unreadable sccache stats) writes no record, so every later sweep retries two cold builds. There is no failure marker.

`sccache --show-stats` label text ('Cache hits', 'Cache misses') is assumed and unit-tested only on sample text. The real `CargoBuild` was not run here: a producer cannot run two full builds. If the labels differ the measurement errors loudly and writes no record.
`git worktree add` writes metadata into the real repository's `.git/worktrees` while a run lasts; it is removed afterwards, including on error.
The sweep pass skips when free disk is below `[disk] min_free_gb` (10 GB by default), the same minimum as dispatch, not a computed need for two builds.
The line label is `build      measurement:`; I did not add it to `STATUS_MEASURE_LABELS` in status.rs.
mistakes: First draft of the disk test compared S with tracked bytes counted after the run, which included the record the run committed; fixed by counting before.
First draft of the NaN refusal test expected `Invalid` from `check_record_file`, but a NaN fails to parse; fixed to assert an error for NaN and `Invalid` for the other bad values.
Ran `cargo test -p athena-cli measure_build` unfiltered across test binaries, printing many empty test blocks and wasting output.
learnings: `AnyRecord` variants must also be handled in `Records::load` in store.rs: its catch-all arm calls `job_of(..).expect(..)` and would panic on any record kind with no job.
`Git::rev_parse` only resolves commits (it appends `^{commit}`), so a file's blob id comes from `ls_tree_under`.
`Records::load` reads the tree at HEAD, and a record committed by `measure_build` is itself a tracked file, so a test must count tracked bytes before the run.
A NaN f64 serializes to JSON null, so a record with a NaN time fails to parse (RecordError::Parse), not Invalid.
The athena-cli display tests build no `StatusView`; an integration test in crates/athena-cli/tests with the `Fixture` helper is the practical way to test `display::status`.
The policy test reads tracked files only, so the new untracked test file was checked by hand against the banned words.
desires: A way to run `cargo test --locked` with a name filter across the whole workspace without 60 'running 0 tests' blocks: the earlier unfiltered output was long and costly.
Confirmation of how the installed `sccache --show-stats` labels its totals; the parser assumes lines `Cache hits` and `Cache misses`.
